messages:
maya: Heads up — our CI SAST just flagged a transitive dependency vendor/foo@3.2.1. It looks like a hardcoded API key in an example. High severity. Can someone triage?
jon: oncall, grabbing the artifact now. can you drop the CI link? also could be just an example in tests. :eyes:
maya: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/1918203045/tar.gz — snippet I saw: ```// TODO: api_key = 'AKIA...'
// examples/usage/example.go``` it's inside `examples/` in the vendor bundle included at build time.
olivia: quick flag — our current suppression workflow lets devs self-approve with a `scan/suppress` label. we should block that for secret-like findings. suppression of secrets must require security reviewer approval (no exceptions).
sam: agreed. also we need to retain scan evidence (scan output + artifact snapshot) for at least 180 days for compliance. plan: push evidence to s3://redwood-scan-evidence/ and encrypt with KMS alias `alias/redwood-scan-evidence`.
security-bot: New vuln triage ticket created: INC-2026-45. Assigned: maya, jon. Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-scan-evidence/1918203045
jon: pulling now. if it's only in examples/testdata we can mark FP, but suppression must go through sec-approval either way. i'll run a quick grep and upload the artifact snapshot to S3.
maya: if suppression happens, require PR template fields: reason, risk assessment, artifact SHA256, link to S3 snapshot (kms-encrypted). also must record approver and timestamp in audit log.
olivia: can we add a pre-merge CI gate that denies `scan/suppress` label unless `sec-approval` label is present and approver belongs to `security-reviewers` org team? sounds like an RBAC change in the GH app.
sam: infra note — KMS integration already in our infra. CI runner needs permission to PutObject/GetObject and kms:Encrypt with alias. example IAM condition snippet I will add to the policy: ```{
  "Sid": "AllowScanCI",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ci-runner"},
  "Action": ["s3:PutObject","s3:GetObject"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-scan-evidence/*",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:KeyAlias": "alias/redwood-scan-evidence"}}
}```
jon: quick question on audit logging: legal mentioned some customers require 3 year retention. do we want default 180d or longer?
maya: default to 180d for platform-level evidence. allow per-customer overrides via ticket (add metadata tag `retention:3y`). for now follow triage runbook: 1) pull artifact, 2) snapshot to S3+KMS, 3) risk assessment, 4) if suppression -> security-reviewers approval + audit entry.
olivia: i'll open the infra PR to add the CI gating and GH app RBAC change, ETA end of day. will also add docs under docs/sec/scan-triage.md describing the new workflow.
sam: i'll create the S3 bucket with lifecycle: 180d -> Glacier, default delete at 3y; update KMS key policy and post it to the ticket.
maya: :thumbsup: jon — paste your grep output & temp S3 link in INC-2026-45 once uploaded. also add the artifact SHA256.
jon: grep shows two matches in vendor/example/testdata. both look like placeholder keys (`AKIA...`) not valid. uploaded snapshot to s3://redwood-scan-evidence/1918203045/artifact.tar.gz (encrypted). SHA256: d2f7c9e4... pasted to ticket. moving state -> triage-in-progress.
security-bot: INC-2026-45 status: triage-in-progress -> evidence-uploaded
